title: Generic pipeline test cues (no lesson content)

cues.text: Welcome to the narration test. This voice should sound relaxed and natural, like a friend talking you through a match.
A formation is only a starting point. Once the game kicks off, the shape keeps changing.
Plenty of teams line up in a 4-2-3-1, with two holding midfielders sitting in front of the back four.
A false nine drops deep from the front line, while a double pivot shields the defence.
The high press is about winning the ball back quickly, high up the pitch, before the other team can settle.
Good choice. That keeps the team compact and leaves very little space between the lines.
Welcome to the audio test. The clips you hear are placeholders, so the words will not describe the movement on screen. The point is to check timing, pausing and captions.
Not quite. Have another look at how the nearby players move to help each other.
That is a common instinct, but it leaves gaps. Watch the next sequence and see where the space opens up.
Red move the ball out wide. Watch how Blue's midfield and defence move across together, keeping their shape.
The nearest midfielder closes down, while the full-back stays behind to provide cover.
On the other side, the winger tucks inside and the back four stay connected. That protects the spaces left by the press.
Red play backwards, so Blue ease off the pressure and settle back into their four-five-one shape.
